主要内容: The article examines the bankruptcies of major energy companies, including Enron, Energy Future Holdings, Pacific Gas & Electric Company, Texaco, and Calpine Corporation. Enron collapsed due to fraudulent accounting, while Energy Future Holdings faced declining revenues and high debt. Pacific Gas & Electric Company struggled with deregulation and fluctuating prices. Texaco faced a legal dispute with Pennzoil, and Calpine incurred massive debt from soaring fuel costs. The article also highlights TP Oil & Gas, which refinanced $1.5 billion in 2009 but faced a 2010 moratorium, leading to $2.7 billion in debt. Patriot Coal, the largest U.S. thermal coal producer, recorded a $198.5 million loss in 2012 due to low prices and environmental rules. James River Coal emerged from bankruptcy in 2004 with $818.7 million in debt. OGX, with $5.1 billion in debt, filed for bankruptcy after failing to negotiate with creditors. Suntech missed a $541 million bond payment due to market glut and collapsing prices. These cases reflect the impact of financial distress, regulatory changes, and market conditions on energy companies.
